name: Belonger Status -- Birth, Descent, or Adoption

qualifying_event.description: A person born in the Virgin Islands to a qualifying parent, born abroad to a Belonger/BOTC parent, or adopted in the Territory by a Belonger, acquires Belonger status under Section 2 of the Virgin Islands Constitution Order 2007.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; parent's proof of Belonger/BOTC status or settled status; adoption order (adoption ground).

requirement_groups.name: Birth in the Territory to a qualifying parent

requirements.blocker_text: Requires birth in the Virgin Islands to a parent who is a BOTC by birth, naturalisation, or registration in the BVI; a person settled in the BVI; or a Belonger by birth or descent (including via a grandparent born in the Territory).

requirement_groups.name: Descent (born abroad to a Belonger/BOTC parent)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a parent who is a Belonger or British Overseas Territories Citizen at the time of the applicant's birth abroad.
Requires adoption in the Territory by a person who is a Belonger by birth or descent.

evidence_required.document: Parent's proof of Belonger/BOTC/settled status, or adoption order

sources.title: Civil Registry and Immigration System of the Virgin Islands (crisvi.gov.vg) -- Belonger status: constitutional grounds under Section 2 of the Virgin Islands Constitution Order 2007 (birth, descent, adoption), and historical 1946 Ordinance provisions (repealed 1969)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the British Virgin Islands' initial build. Three constitutional grounds folded into one file as OR-groups since all three grant the identical Belonger status outcome directly under Section 2 of the Constitution Order, without the discretionary Cabinet assessment or 20-year tenure required by vg_belonger_status_residence.json. IMPORTANT: per the source, Belonger status does NOT automatically pass from parent to child -- a child of a newly-Belonger parent must separately apply upon reaching 18, or register under the British Nationality Act; this is flagged rather than modelled as automatic inheritance. See vg_belonger_status_residence.json's notes for why leads_to_citizenship is modelled as true (Belonger status is itself one of the five BOTC naturalisation fee categories) while being a distinct status from actual British nationality.
